headline: High: n8n’s default server-side execution and broad egress can leak or act on Argo outputs unless the workflow is tightly isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo can emit workflow artifacts over REST/gRPC, and n8n can ingest files and API outputs into workflow nodes. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if n8n treats Argo-produced content as trusted. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low because the shared workflow surface exists by default.
conditions: IF n8n workflow nodes parse Argo-generated artifacts as instructions or prompts
IF Argo outputs are copied into n8n without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter/schema for Argo outputs before n8n parses them
Require manual review for any prompt-like text from Argo
Strip executable directives from workflow artifacts
Use a separate staging file for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Argo and n8n

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and has broad network egress. If Argo outputs sensitive artifacts into n8n’s workspace, n8n can transmit them through integrations or external APIs. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters contain sensitive data
IF n8n workflows send those files or fields to external integrations
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Disable or gate outbound integrations for sensitive runs
Mask secrets before handing artifacts to n8n
Review credential scopes for each integration node
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on workflow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo can call APIs and n8n can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the server filesystem. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared external systems through overlapping API and filesystem actions. The conflict is real in default deployments, but not as severe as same-dir unrestricted write plus git locking failures.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or external API resource
IF n8n Execute Command writes files that Argo later consumes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared resources with a lock file
Disable Execute Command for shared-state workflows
Use idempotent API operations where possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce artifacts and parameters that n8n workflows may consume as inputs, and n8n can then trigger downstream integrations or commands. If n8n treats Argo output as authoritative, a bad upstream value can cascade into irreversible external actions. The interaction is inferred from documented workflow chaining, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n uses Argo-produced fields as decision inputs without validation
IF downstream n8n nodes send emails, update systems, or execute commands
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Argo and n8n
Require human approval before action nodes run
Constrain n8n to read-only inspection for Argo outputs
Log and diff upstream values before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts for inter-agent handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Argo’s docs-only profile does not specify residency or retention, while n8n stores credentials on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for regulated data classes, but the evidence is indirect and not enough for high. I cite both because the compliance risk arises from their combined handling model.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF n8n retention or credential storage exceeds the policy applied to Argo artifacts
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Set explicit retention limits in n8n
Purge workflow execution logs after use
Store secrets only in approved credential stores
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
